title: Magnetic Storage
description: A disk stores each bit in a few dozen magnetic grains. Smaller grains pack more bits, but a grain's will to keep its direction is its anisotropy times its volume, and the warmth of the room keeps trying to flip it: shrink it far enough and the data evaporates, the superparamagnetic limit. The way past is a harder magnet, iron platinum, too hard for any head to write until a laser heats each spot near its Curie point. Unlocks the Media Sputter Chamber.

puzzle.goal: A grain of volume V and anisotropy K must climb an energy barrier K·V to flip, at temperature T. With the attempt time τ₀ and Boltzmann's k, write how long it keeps its bit, t (Néel and Arrhenius).
puzzle.name: Néel relaxation time
puzzle.form: τ * exp ( K * V / ( k * T ) )
puzzle.expr: tau * exp ( K * V / ( k * T ) )
puzzle.ask: Find t in seconds for τ₀ = 10⁻⁹ s, K·V = 40kT at T = @{T} K.
puzzle.method: The chance each attempt succeeds is the Boltzmann factor e^(−KV/kT); the wait is one attempt time over it.
